title: Equipment write-off: ordered by Dec 31 isn't enough
label: Year-end tax move

lines: Dev orders a new printer on Dec. 20.
It arrives and gets set up Jan. 5.
Can he write it off for 2026?

beats.sub: Ready and available to use by Dec. 31.

beats.note: Bonus: property acquired after Jan. 19, 2025. State rules can differ.

items.t: Get it delivered and set up

cta.sub: We'll DM you our Section 179 guide.

captions.instagram:
Buying equipment to write off for 2026? The date that matters isn't the order date.

✔️ The IRS ties the deduction to the year the asset is placed in service: ready and available for its use.
✔️ Ordered Dec. 20, set up Jan. 5? That's generally a 2027 asset.
✔️ 2026 federal limits: Section 179 up to $2,560,000, and 100% bonus depreciation for property acquired after Jan. 19, 2025.
✔️ Section 179 needs more than 50% business use in that first year.

State rules can differ. Our Section 179 guide walks through both options.
captions.youtube_title: Section 179 Before Dec 31: Ordering Isn't Enough
captions.youtube_description: Equipment counts for the year it's placed in service, meaning ready and available for its use, not the year you order it. 2026 federal limits: Section 179 up to $2,560,000 and 100% bonus depreciation for property acquired after Jan. 19, 2025. Section 179 needs over 50% business use. State rules can differ.
captions.pinterest_title: Section 179 Deduction 2026: Equipment Must Be Placed in Service by December 31
captions.pinterest_description: Section 179 and bonus depreciation for 2026: equipment counts in the year it's placed in service, not when it's ordered. The 2026 Section 179 limit is $2,560,000 and 100% bonus depreciation is back for property acquired after Jan. 19, 2025. Set it up by Dec. 31, note the date and keep the invoice.
captions.pinterest_alt: Short video: a business owner orders equipment in December; it explains the placed-in-service rule and the 2026 Section 179 and bonus depreciation limits.
captions.pinterest_board: Tax Write Offs & Deductions for Small Business

sources.fact: You place property in service when it is ready and available for a specific use; Section 179 is deducted in the year placed in service; Section 179 only if used more than 50% for business in that year (Pub 946, 2025); read 2026-10-30

2026: Section 179 limit $2,560,000, phase-out above $4,090,000, SUV limit $32,000; QBI threshold $201,750 (single) / $403,500 (MFJ); $400 minimum QBI deduction with at least $1,000 of QBI (Rev. Proc. 2025-32); read 2026-10-30
Permanent 100% additional first-year depreciation for eligible property acquired after Jan. 19, 2025 (IR-2026-06, Jan. 14, 2026; Notice 2026-11); read 2026-10-30
